\chapter{First Food Words: No New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-food-three}
\hlchaptermodality{23}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can retrieve lentils, clarified butter, and vegetables in listening, speaking, reading, and writing using only previously taught Devanagari signs.}

Three source-attested food words begin by ear, add no new sign at all, and close in a non-compensatory four-skill payoff.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dāl]{Hear \emph{dāl} — lentils}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-hear-daal}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word transport payoff, then say horse and market.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{dāl} — \textbf{lentils}
\end{quote}

Two beats, and the second one is long. Hear it twice, point to a bowl of cooked lentils, and say it once. The spelling stays covered until the sound and the meaning are comfortable.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dāl]{\mw{दाल} — lentils on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-daal}



\begin{quote}
Say lentils, then write horse and \textbf{\mw{ज}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{दा}} + \textbf{\mw{ल}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{दाल}} — \emph{dāl} — lentils
\end{quote}

Three units, all of them met before: \textbf{\mw{द}}, the long \textbf{\mw{ा}}, and \textbf{\mw{ल}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{दाल}}. Check that the \textbf{\mw{ा}} sits after \textbf{\mw{द}} and not after \textbf{\mw{ल}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghī]{Hear \emph{ghī} — clarified butter}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-hear-ghee}



\begin{quote}
Recall the seven-word shopping payoff, then write lentils and market.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{ghī} — \textbf{clarified butter}
\end{quote}

One beat, opening with the same breathy sound heard at the start of \emph{ghar} and \emph{ghoṛo}. Hear it twice and say it once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghī]{\mw{घी} — clarified butter on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-ghee}



\begin{quote}
Say clarified butter, recall the five-word transport payoff, then say bus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{घ}} + \textbf{\mw{ी}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{घी}} — \emph{ghī} — clarified butter
\end{quote}

The same \textbf{\mw{घ}} that opens \textbf{\mw{घर}} and \textbf{\mw{घोड़ो}}, carrying the long \textbf{\mw{ी}} met in \textbf{\mw{पाणी}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{घी}}. Keep the \textbf{\mw{ी}} stroke tall enough to reach the headline.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sabjī]{Hear \emph{sabjī} — vegetables}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-hear-sabji}



\begin{quote}
Write clarified butter, bus, and \textbf{\mw{घ}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{sabjī} — \textbf{vegetables}
\end{quote}

Three beats, ending long. Hear it twice, point to a vegetable dish, and say it once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sabjī]{\mw{सबजी} — vegetables on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-sabji}



\begin{quote}
Say vegetables and vehicle, then write home.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{स}} + \textbf{\mw{ब}} + \textbf{\mw{जी}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{सबजी}} — \emph{sabjī} — vegetables
\end{quote}

Four units, every one of them already in the hand. The source spells it with a full \textbf{\mw{ब}} between \textbf{\mw{स}} and \textbf{\mw{जी}}; other Rajasthani writing prints a clustered spelling for the same word, so treat this form as the one attested here rather than as the only one anybody uses.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{सबजी}}. Check that \textbf{\mw{ब}} keeps its own short vowel and carries no vowel-killer.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve three food words}

\label{lesson:MW-R18-food-three}



\begin{quote}
Write vehicle, then say temple and home.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the three words in a mixed order, give each meaning, read three shuffled cards, then write all three from sound.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.

\section[Practice]{Payoff — three food words in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C18-food-three}



\begin{quote}
Say cart, then write temple.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify three heard words. 2. Produce three words from meaning cues. 3. Match three printed cards to meanings. 4. Write all three heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately. Three food names are a vocabulary foundation, not an order placed in a kitchen or a shop.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-6-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 6}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the first food loop}

\label{lesson:MW-R18-food-close}

Recall the three-place payoff, then write cart.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
With every model hidden, identify, say, read, and write \textbf{\mw{दाल}}, \textbf{\mw{घी}}, and \textbf{\mw{सबजी}} in a shuffled order.
